The working directory is actually empty — there's no `misc` or `utils` folder here for me to inspect, so I can't base this on your real file list. I'll give you a proposed structure based on the categories you described; you (or I, once pointed at the real repo) can slot the actual files in.

**Proposed structure**

```
scripts/
  migrations/        # one-off migration scripts
config/
  templates/         # config templates
docs/
  compliance/        # archived compliance reports
  meeting-notes/      # old meeting notes (or consider deleting if stale)
shared/
  <lib-name>/        # shared helper functions used by 2+ services, grouped by purpose
services/
  <service>/lib/     # helpers used by only one service move back into that service
```

For `utils`, rather than one grouping, split by what the helpers actually operate on — e.g. `shared/http/`, `shared/date/`, `shared/validation/`, `shared/testing/` — so each subfolder has a clear single responsibility instead of being another catch-all.

Rules of thumb to keep it from re-rotting:
- Nothing lands in a top-level "misc"/"utils" again — if it doesn't fit an existing category, that's a signal to create a properly named one.
- Anything used by only one service belongs in that service's own directory, not a shared one.
- Stuff that's just historical record (old meeting notes, superseded compliance reports) goes to `docs/archive/` or gets deleted, not mixed in with active code.

If you can point me at the actual repo path (or run this from inside the real repo directory), I can list the real 47 + 30 files, categorize each one concretely, and give you the exact `git mv` commands to do the reorg.
